title: Rabies Risk Needs Quarantine—and Dog-Trade Abolition by 2030
excerpt: Uninspected slaughter and secret animal movement create preventable risks. Rabies exposure demands urgent care; Vietnam needs transparent enforcement and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A bite, scratch, or infected saliva entering broken skin can become a race against rabies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. That danger exists beside another failure: unregulated slaughter and animal movement can bypass inspection, quarantine, and community protection.

Tradition Cannot Replace Traceability

“Farm-raised dogs” is a claim, not proof. A lawful supply chain would require traceable origin, veterinary oversight, transport controls, quarantine compliance, and inspected slaughter. Informal trade cannot earn public trust by repeating tradition while withholding records that verify origin and health status.

Public Health Starts Before Exposure

Rabies does not spread through properly cooked meat as an established route. Risk involves infected saliva from bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes, along with handling sick animals and uninspected slaughter. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes. Seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Care must begin before symptoms develop. WHO guidance explains why delay can cost a life.

Vietnamese Communities Can Close the Gap

Household rabies prevention and commercial-trade regulation are separate duties. Both require enforcement, transparent records, and protection for families. Official rabies-control targets are not the same as SDE’s demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Sign the national petition calling for nationwide abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition, add your name to a public demand for action, and follow campaign updates reaching decision-makers.

Rabies control cannot stop at household gates. It must include every point where sick animals may be handled, moved, or slaughtered without inspection.

Rabies exposure occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical care. Vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies must be given before symptoms develop. WHO guidance: https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/rabies

Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route. The public-health concern lies in sick animals, unsafe handling, uninspected slaughter, and movement that defeats traceability and quarantine.

“Farm-raised” cannot remain an evidence-free defense. Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, and local authorities deserve records, enforcement, and protection from illicit operators. Official rabies-control targets and SDE’s abolition demand are distinct: SDE calls for complete abolition by 2030.
